topic: Fundamental Rights (Part III) of Indian Polity
description: Part III of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 12 to 35, deals with Fundamental Rights. Inspired by the Bill of Rights of the US Constitution, this part is often described as the 'Magna Carta of India' and guarantees civil liberties to all citizens.

sections.title: Introduction and General Articles
sections.description: The nature of Fundamental Rights, the definition of 'State', and the doctrine of judicial review for inconsistent laws.

polity_articles.details: The 'State' includes the Government and Parliament of India, State Governments and Legislatures, and all local or other authorities within the territory of India.

polity_articles.provision: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights
polity_articles.details: Declares that all laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights shall be void. It provides the constitutional basis for the doctrine of Judicial Review.

important_facts.fact: Originally, the Constitution provided for 7 Fundamental Rights, but currently, there are only 6.
Fundamental Rights available ONLY to Indian Citizens (and not foreigners): Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30.
Fundamental Rights are not absolute; the State can impose 'reasonable restrictions' on them on grounds like state security, public order, and morality.

sections.title: Right to Equality (Articles 14-18)
sections.description: Guarantees equality before the law, prohibits discrimination, and abolishes untouchability and titles.

polity_articles.provision: Equality before Law and Equal Protection of Laws
polity_articles.details: 'Equality before Law' is of British origin, whereas 'Equal Protection of Laws' has been taken from the American Constitution.
Prohibits discrimination by the State against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.

polity_articles.provision: Equality of opportunity in public employment
polity_articles.details: Ensures equal opportunity for all citizens in matters of employment under the State, with provisions for reservation for backward classes.
Abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form. It is a punishable offence in accordance with the law.
Prohibits the State from conferring any titles except those for military or academic distinctions (e.g., Bharat Ratna, Padma awards are not titles).

sections.title: Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22)
sections.description: Provides basic democratic freedoms and safeguards for life, personal liberty, and against arbitrary arrest.

polity_articles.details: Guarantees freedom of: (a) speech and expression, (b) peaceful assembly, (c) forming associations, (d) free movement, (e) residence, and (g) profession or trade.

polity_articles.provision: Protection in respect of conviction for offences
polity_articles.details: Grants protection against ex-post-facto laws (retrospective criminal law), double jeopardy (punished twice for the same offence), and self-incrimination.

polity_articles.provision: Protection of life and personal liberty
polity_articles.details: States that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to the 'procedure established by law'.
Makes elementary education a Fundamental Right, mandating the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.
Grants the right to be informed of grounds of arrest, the right to consult a lawyer, and the right to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.

sections.title: Rights against Exploitation & Freedom of Religion (Articles 23-28)
sections.description: Prohibits human trafficking and forced labor, and guarantees the freedom to practice and propagate religion.

polity_articles.provision: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labor
polity_articles.details: Prohibits selling/buying of human beings, 'begar' (unpaid labor), and other similar forms of forced labor.

polity_articles.provision: Prohibition of employment of children in factories
polity_articles.details: No child below the age of 14 years shall be employed to work in any factory, mine, or engaged in any other hazardous employment.

polity_articles.provision: Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion
polity_articles.details: Subject to public order, morality, and health, all persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
Grants every religious denomination the right to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes.

important_facts.fact: Article 27 ensures freedom from paying taxes for the promotion of any specific religion, and Article 28 prohibits religious instruction in state-funded educational institutions.

sections.title: Cultural, Educational & Constitutional Remedies (Articles 29-32)
sections.description: Protects minority linguistic/cultural rights and empowers citizens to move the Supreme Court for rights enforcement.

polity_articles.details: Any section of the citizens residing in India having a distinct language, script, or culture of its own has the right to conserve the same.

polity_articles.provision: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
polity_articles.details: All minorities, whether based on religion or language, have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'. It allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

key_concepts.explanation: Literally means 'to have the body of'. Issued by a court to a person who has detained another, directing them to produce the detainee before the court.
Literally means 'we command'. Issued to a public official directing them to perform their official duties that they have failed or refused to perform.
Issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal either to transfer a case pending with the latter to itself or to quash the order of the latter.
Literally means 'by what authority or warrant'. Issued to inquire into the legality of a person's claim to a public office.

sections.title: Exceptions and Important Amendments
sections.description: Modifications of rights for armed forces, martial law scenarios, and key constitutional amendments.

polity_articles.details: Empowers Parliament to restrict or abrogate the Fundamental Rights of armed forces, police forces, and intelligence agencies to ensure the proper discharge of their duties.
Provides for the restriction on Fundamental Rights while martial law (military rule) is in force in any area within the territory of India.
Deleted the Right to Property (Article 31) from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a normal Constitutional/Legal Right under Article 300A in Part XII.

important_facts.fact: During a National Emergency (Article 352), all Fundamental Rights can be suspended EXCEPT the rights guaranteed by Articles 20 and 21.
The six freedoms guaranteed under Article 19 can only be suspended when an emergency is declared on the grounds of 'war or external aggression', and not on the grounds of 'armed rebellion'.
